title: How to Build a Refund Approval Workflow (2026 Guide)
summary: A refund approval workflow helps finance teams establish automated verification steps to prevent unauthorized losses and streamline customer service.
body_markdown:
## Building the refund workflow in Activepieces step-by-step


Activepieces handles custom refund logic by connecting your payment processor to a visual canvas. AI-generated steps bridge the gap between standard transaction data and your specific business rules, drawing from a library of 748 integrations to reach your existing stack.


While most platforms limit you to a fixed library of templates, Activepieces uses a built-in AI chat to construct the exact logic you describe.


If your refund policy requires a unique sequence (like creating a HubSpot task and alerting a Slack owner only after a second failed Stripe payment) you can simply state that requirement to have the platform build and publish the flow.


This removes the template catalog as the ceiling for what your finance team can automate.


### Selecting the stripe 'refund created' integration


The workflow begins by selecting Stripe, a financial infrastructure platform, as the trigger source. This ensures every initiated refund is captured the moment it hits your ledger.


In the Activepieces builder, you drag the Stripe integration onto the canvas and select the "Refund Created" event. This establishes a webhook listener that fires whenever a customer or staff member triggers a return.


Roughly **60% of these integrations** are community-contributed, ensuring that even niche financial events are often already supported.


The canvas displays this as a "New Lead" or "New Event" trigger. It provides the raw JSON payload required for the subsequent logic steps.


### Adding the 'wait for approval' action


You insert a "Human Approval" step immediately after the trigger to prevent automated systems from draining your liquidity on suspicious or high-value edge cases. This step pauses the execution of the workflow and generates a unique approval URL.


You then route this URL to a Slack notification so that a manager can verify the return without leaving their chat interface. Activepieces provides a built-in "Wait for Approval" integration that holds the state of the flow until a maximum wait duration is reached.


You aren't billed for execution time while waiting for a human.


The run is the meter, not the steps inside it. A complex ten-step refund validation costs the same single credit as a two-step notification, which you can verify on the published pricing page: **1 credit per flow run** , regardless of step count.


### Testing the workflow with live data


The final stage involves running a sample execution through the canvas to verify that the DeepSeek-v4-pro or Claude Sonnet 5.5 models you’ve integrated for risk scoring are correctly interpreting the Stripe metadata.


By clicking "Test Step," Activepieces pulls the most recent transaction from your live Stripe account. This allows you to see exactly how the "Qualified?" condition handles a real-world refund amount.


If the test fails, the logs pinpoint exactly which integration returned an error code. You can then fix the logic before the first customer actually requests a return.
